name: Consentmo
summary: Shopify consent app that geolocates the visitor and shows the right GDPR, CCPA, PIPEDA or LGPD banner, with Google Consent Mode v2 and Meta, Microsoft and TikTok signals, cookie scanning and data-request pages, plus an accessibility widget and scanner from the Plus tier. Banner impressions are unlimited on every tier.
best_for: Shopify merchants selling into several jurisdictions who want one app to carry the cookie banner, the consent signals the ad platforms now demand, and a first layer of accessibility, and who go in knowing that the region-aware banner and the accessibility tools sit on the $37 tier.
skip_if: you sell outside Shopify; you need one plain cookie banner in one country, which the free tier or your theme already covers; or you need an actual accessibility audit and repair of your theme rather than a widget and a scanner.
honest_knock: Read the ladder before you budget $10 for this. The two things the listing leads with (web accessibility and a smart region-specific banner) are not on Standard; they start at Plus, $37 a month, which is 3.7 times the entry price. The top plan is now Max at $99 a month (Shopify listing, 27 Nov 2026), and the listing does not name a checkout banner for Shopify Plus or headless support, so ask Consentmo before you buy for those. The accessibility side is a widget and a scanner: it overlays controls and flags issues, but it does not change the theme markup underneath, which is where an accessibility audit actually looks: treat it as a first layer, not as a remediation. And the free tier puts Consentmo's own branding on the banner your visitors see first.

pricing.plans_source: hand-curated from the vendor's pricing page
pricing.notes: (read 2026-09-08 on apps.shopify.com/gdpr-backpack and on the vendor's own consentmo.com/pricing, which list the same four tiers) Billed in USD every 30 days, with a 7-day free trial on each paid tier. Banner impressions are unlimited on every tier, the free one included, so the ladder gates features rather than traffic. Free costs nothing and covers the cookie banner and preferences, the data-request and Do-Not-Sell pages, one banner language and one cookie scan a month, with minimal Consentmo branding on the banner. Standard is $10 a month or $100 a year (17% off) and adds unlimited cookie scans, multi-region compliance (GDPR, CCPA, PIPEDA and others), Google Consent Mode v2 and Meta, Microsoft and TikTok integrations, US opt-out signals, script blocking, multilingual banners with automatic detection, automatic Google Drive backups and removal of the branding. Plus is $37 or $370 a year and is where the accessibility side starts: web accessibility (ADA/WCAG), smart geotargeting, the EU withdrawal page for Directive 2023/2673, automated monitoring, scheduled scans, AI cookie categorisation, advanced analytics and full CSS customisation. The Shopify listing read on 27 November 2026 names the top plan Max at $99 a month or $990 a year, with consent monitoring, proof of consent, banner statistics, a privacy centre, an alt-text manager, IAB TCF 2.4 compliance and bot protection; the earlier top plan, Enterprise at $64 a month, is no longer listed.

compare_with.name: accessiBe
compare_with.why: these two only look alike on the accessibility line. accessiBe sells accessibility as its whole product, on any site, and goes deeper than a widget; Consentmo sells consent as its whole product and adds accessibility from the $37 tier up. So if accessibility is the reason you are shopping, Consentmo's Plus tier is a starting layer rather than a replacement. If consent is the reason, the two are not in the same market at all: the cookie banner, the geotargeting and the Consent Mode integrations are what Consentmo is for, and they are not what accessiBe sells

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Consentmo GDPR on a Shopify development store: the install, the three-step onboarding with a banner preview, the plan screen with a Black Friday promotion, the Shopify approval screen for Standard (not approved), the Free plan, one click on Activate for the app embed, the banner in the theme editor preview and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was paid and nothing was saved in the theme editor. Install: the App Store listing (English) is called Consentmo GDPR and says Free plan available. Free trial available. The first install try at about 12:21 ended with Installation canceled.; the second try opened a pop-up tab with only the list of apps; the third try opened the Install app dialog in the admin, which asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data. Install was approved at about 12:23 and the app opened on its dashboard. Onboarding: three steps, Choose your region (Europe, GDPR), Design your cookie banner and Set your consent options (Accept / Reject / Preferences, marked Popular), ending with the button Finish set up. In step 3 the app shows a preview as Europe with the text We use cookies to run this site, measure traffic, and personalize content. and the buttons Preferences, Reject and Accept. Core action: Finish set up led straight to the plan screen Pick your plan. Back on the dashboard it said Current plan: Free, Cookie banner: Setup needed and App embed is not enabled. One click on Activate gave the message Cookie bar enabled on your store., so the app embed was switched on by the app itself in one click, without a theme edit by us. The dashboard then showed Cookie Consent Health 71 / 100 with 6 issues, among them EU Withdrawal page not set up, Google Consent Mode v2 not configured and Cookie Policy page missing, Banner visible: Europe and Smart Geotargeting: Off. In the theme editor the banner showed on the home page preview with the same text and the buttons Preferences, Reject and Accept; nothing was saved in the theme editor and the storefront outside the editor was not opened. Timing, approximate tester observations: about 2 minutes from the install (12:23) to the banner in the theme editor preview (about 12:25), in about 7 steps (choose region, Next, Next, Finish set up, back to the dashboard, Activate, open the editor). The first try at 12:21 and the second try were wasted by install errors. Plans: the Pick your plan screen is monthly by default and carries the label BFCM Deal: 25% Off for 3 Months. Free $0 a month (Get started); Standard $7.5 a month, was $10.00; Plus $27.75, was $37.00, marked Most popular; Max $74.25, was $99.00; each paid plan has Start 7-day FREE trial, and Pay annually carries the label 2 months free. The comparison table lists Free $0, Standard $10, Plus $37 and Max $99 a month. Free: unlimited impressions, cookie banner and preferences, Privacy Center, Do Not Sell page and 1 scan a month. Standard: Integrations (Google Consent v2, Meta + more), Multi-region compliance, Unlimited cookie scans, Multilingual banner and No Consentmo branding. Plus: Web Accessibility, Smart Geotargeting, EU Withdrawal and Age gate. Max: Consent monitoring, Proof of consent and IAB TCF 2.4. Under the plans a box says Managing more than one store? We offer custom pricing for brands and agencies managing multiple Shopify stores. with a Chat with us button, which we did not press. Checkout: Start 7-day FREE trial on Standard opened the Shopify Approve subscription screen: Consentmo GDPR by Consentmo, $2,50 off 3 charges, plan Standard, $10,00 struck through and $7,50 USD every 30 days, You have a 7-day free trial ending on 24 Nov., subtotal $10,00 plus any applicable taxes, discount $2,50 off -$2,50, total $7,50 due 24 Nov., and an Add payment method row. The sentence about a test charge was NOT on this screen and Approve was greyed out, so we did not approve; no card was entered. The Cancel button did not react, so we went back to the dashboard by navigation. The Free plan stayed active without any approval screen. Cancelling: no subscription ran, because the Free plan was used. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, the menu of the app with Open app, View details, Get support and Uninstall; the dialog Uninstall Consentmo GDPR? says you will no longer be able to use the app, that any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. A reason is required before the button works; we chose Testing multiple apps. Not tested: the Standard features (Google Consent Mode v2, the Meta, Microsoft and TikTok signals and script blocking, because the plan needed a payment method), Plus (accessibility, EU Withdrawal page, Smart Geotargeting) and Max, a price for a second store, the cookie scan, generating a privacy page and annual prices. Clean up: the app embed was switched on with the Activate button of the app (the only setting we changed); no theme was saved in the theme editor. The app was uninstalled after the test with the reason Testing multiple apps. Our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The first two install tries failed, the plan screen shows promotion prices for 3 months that are lower than the list prices, the Standard approval screen asks for a payment method and has no test charge sentence, the Cancel button on that screen did not react, and the dashboard of the Free plan starts at a health score of 71 with 6 open issues.
